title: scheduler configuration
description: Every tunable of the Go scheduler (SPEC-16.G g-keys). Every key is required and no other key is allowed, because Go holds no default (g-nodefault). Keys are flat and dotted, exactly as g-keys spells them: the registry names both seat (a string) and seat.busy_regex and its siblings, so nesting by the dot would put two values under one name; flat keys also make the loader's error name the key as the spec does. Strings may carry ${repo}, ${state_dir}, ${host_repo}, ${HOME} or ${ENV:NAME}, resolved by the loader at start (g-vars); every path value starts with one of them, so no host path is written here. This file validates before resolution, so mode and herdr_session accept their ENV form. No $schema keyword: the directory's test plan greps every file here for a scheme separator, and jsonschema validates an unmarked schema with its newest draft, 2020-12, the draft every config schema in this repo names.

env.description: exactly one environment variable, set by the run wrapper, the only place that knows the host (SPEC-16.H h-run-env)

path.description: a path that starts with a variable, so the file lifts to another host unchanged (g-vars-portable)

seat.description: a seat name as events/schema/event.schema.json accepts it

mode.description: off, shadow or active (SPEC-16.J j-mode); an ENV variable so the pane wrapper sets it, and the loader checks the resolved value against the three words

seat.description: the scheduler's seat on every record it writes; must equal executor.json seat, which the record verb forces

herdr_session.description: the herdr session the executor addresses; same variable as executor.json herdr_session

repo.description: the repository as mounted in the container, for reading (g-vars-two-repos)

host_repo.description: the repository on the host, used only in text typed or run there; COQ_REPO is the name the host shell and executor.json already use for it

state_dir.description: ledger, jobs, latches, belt, shadow; the shadow's own in shadow mode and the bash belt's when active (SPEC-16.J j-active-adopt), so the wrapper sets it

playbooks_dir.description: a host path: it is written on the wake line the seat reads, so it hangs off host_repo, not repo

halt_flag.description: the same file herdr/config/herdr.json names (its state_dir plus HALT), because the supervisor reads the same flag (SPEC-16.F f-halt)

drain_seconds.description: how long running jobs may finish at shutdown

intake.poll_seconds.description: seconds between ticks; the bound matches factory/config/runner.json poll_seconds

intake.roots.description: root patterns in priority order, globs allowed; the first is the checkout's log (SPEC-16.A a-roots)

intake.runner_seats.description: seats whose records are own: the scheduler's seat and the bash runner's seat (factory/config/runner.json runner_seat)

seat.busy_regex.description: pane footer pattern meaning busy, as herdr/bin/turnwatch.sh matches it

seat.done_regex.description: pane footer pattern meaning a turn ended, as herdr/bin/turnwatch.sh matches it

seat.absent_wait_seconds.description: at least the supervisor's re-seat window (herdr/config/herdr.json reseat.window_seconds), so a prompt outlives one re-seat

retry.jitter.description: fraction of a delay added or removed; below 1 so a delay never reaches zero

wake.ack_seconds.description: confirmation window per role; the loader checks every role file in roles_dir has one (g-val-cross), so the role list lives in roles/ and nowhere here

stall.deadline_seconds.description: stall deadline per gate kind; the loader checks every kind in the flow file's gates has one (g-val-cross)

stall.visible_within_seconds.description: the loader refuses a file whose intake.poll_seconds plus the smallest deadline passes this bound

belt.file.description: the name the bash runner uses under its state dir (factory/bin/route.sh BELT), so going active continues the same file

belt.stale_seconds.description: the bound of factory/config/runner.json stale_seconds, because the status words and comparison are the bash runner's

executor.socket.description: the executor socket as mounted in the container; the wrapper mounts the runtime dir at the same path

executor.health_seconds.description: at most intake.poll_seconds, checked by the loader

control.socket.description: the scheduler's own unix socket, in the state directory (SPEC-16.H h-proto-sockets)

housekeeping.glass_sweep_seconds.description: 15 is the period of today's glass watcher loop in herdr/config/monitors.json
